(= Pali id.; Skt. in other mgs.), distress, trouble, adversity: ye … utpadyetsuḥ āśravā vighātā paridāghā … (in Pali also foll. by pariḷāha); esp. used of the needs of poor (‘needy’) people: vighāto me cīvareṇa … pātreṇa … glānabhaiṣajyena, (, I am worried about, but it really means) I need a robe, etc., said by a monk to a wealthy patron; ˚ta-kṛtaṃ (dānavipratibandhahetuṃ; in 8, duḥkhaṃ); vighātārthika (cf. vighātin with arthin), a petitioner, beggar, in distress, ˚ka-yuktaṃ … dānaṃ, ˚ka-dānam 14; ˚kaṃ, prob. error for [Page483-b] ˚ka-, dānaṃ, resumed by ˚ka-dānaṃ 10; others, in cpds., see Index.

(to next, n. act.; gives ˚na, but without convincing evidence), dissuasion, determent: mahāyānaprasthitānāṃ ca sattvānā(ṃ) ˚nā; vicchandanāyāpi (read ˚nā yāpi) ca buddhayānaṃ (read ˚nād, abl.? so Tib., -las) id. 6 (vs), referring to 3 above, must surely mean and dissuasion from the Buddha-vehicle; ˚danayā (so read with v.l. for text ˚danatayā) ca striyaḥ strībhāvābhiratānāṃ ca strībhāvāt; tatparasya ˚danārthaṃ; duṣkaracaryādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ vicchandanārthaṃ (misprinted).

, for which forms of vi-chind- occur [Page484-b] in mss., cf. also vicchindika and prec.; see (mss. vary in between a and i); in Pali (kāya-)vicchinda occurs as title of, surely meaning aversion from the body, not cutting off of …; in atidānato vicchinditukāmo clearly means wanting to dissuade from over-generosity, = BHS vi-chand-; Pali (kāya-)vicchandaniya(-kathā) and (kāya-)vicchandanika- (-sutta) cannot be separated from (kāya-)vicchinda, above; in even the v.l. vicchedayām āsuḥ occurs for vicchandayām āsuḥ. It is clear that Pali and BHS both show what must, therefore, be a very old confusion between chand- and -chi(n)d- here. As (cited s.v. vicchinda),, and some others have seen, the orig. form was surely vicchandayati; the forms with chi(n)d- are due to popular etym. (in some occurrences the word means something close to cuts off). The fundamental mg. is makes undesirous (denom., vi plus chanda); so Tib. mos pa zlog pa on, ḥdun pa zlog on, both mg. desire-deterring, desire-dissuading, but on simply zlog par byed pa, dissuasion-(deterring-)making: ˚dayati, foll. by vicakṣuḥ-karaṇāya; bhūyobhūyaḥ sa māṃ ˚dayati, bhadramukhāniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇo phalavipākaḥ, similarly, dissuades; ˚dayām āsuḥ (v.l. see above); (Māraḥ …) bodhisattvaṃ … evaṃ ˚dayiṣyati, will (try to) dissuade; (iha … bodhisattvasya … pāpamitraṃ, yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ) carantaṃ virecayati (q.v.) vichandayati, modulated in the sequel (the means of dissuasion are given; they consist of attacks on the dogmatic interpretation of Buddhism accepted in this school); (devaputrāḥ … Māraṃ …) vicchandayanti and (prose), dissuade, discourage Māra (by predicting his defeat); ˚dayati vikṣipati; when the thing dissuaded from is expressed it is regularly abl., dānād vicchandayan; (saṃgrahavastubhyo) vicchandya; adattādānād ˚dayati; vichandya (v.l. vichindya) with ablatives, so also ˚dayet; ˚dayati (v.l. ˚chind˚); but once apparently acc., (yasmāt tvaṃ bhikṣucaraṇapranāmaṃ) māṃ ˚dayitum icchasi, since you wish to dissuade me (against, from) bowing at the feet of monks (or is this acc. a Bhvr. adj., me characterized by bowing etc.?).

(2), expl. by iṣṭahetutvena in comm., in by akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām apāyeṣu vipāko vipacyate, kuśala-sāsravāṇāṃ sugatau; -karma-samādāna-hetuso-vipākaso-(for ˚śo; according to causes and results)-jñāna-; dattvā ca vipākāpratikāṅkṣī, not looking for ‘maturation’ i.e. recompense, reward (for the gift.)

, adj. (to vipāka plus -ya), coming to fruition: dvaidha-vi˚.
, adj., ˚kaḥ, in a list describing bodily characteristics, esp. unusual ones or deformities; acc. to Tib. lus glebs pa ḥdra ba, with body like something flat; Chin. body like a flat platter.

(see next: for Pali vipiṭṭhikatvā(na) see pṛṣṭhībhavati), (1) makes depressed, discourages: na viṣādam āpatsyate na vipṛṣṭhīkariṣyati mānasam; (2) (cf. pṛṣṭhībhavati 1) turns oneʼs back on, abandons:, see s.v. chorayati (8).

(cf. prec., and s.v. pṛṣṭhībhavati), becomes depressed, discouraged, = pṛṣṭhībhavati (2): (na viṣādam āpadyate) nāsya vipṛṣṭhībhavati mānasaṃ; (cittaṃ nāvalīyate na saṃlīyate,) na vipṛṣṭhībhavati asya mānasam.

, adj. (vi, neg., plus Skt. pra˚; cf. Pali appakampin), not subject to being disturbed: sukhaduḥkhavi˚, … by pleasure or pain, of the Buddhaʼs body, in a long series of epithets of it; not oscillating between bliss and suffering, claiming support of Chin. for not oscillating; at least Chin. seems to support the neg. (= vi).
, ppp. (= Pali vippakata), interrupted, uncompleted: pārājikakathā na ˚tā bhavati (cf. Pali);.
, nt. (n. act. to next; not recorded), departure: tūṣṇīṃ ˚ṇam.

(= Pali vippakkamati; cf. prec.), departs, goes away: asmiṃ (sc. tathāgate) janapadacārikāṃ vā viprakrānte parinirvṛte vā, and when he has gone away on a journey over the countryside, or has entered nirvāṇa …; ˚kram˚; ˚krām˚.
(m.), destruction, slaying: tau parasparam eva mahājana-˚taṃ kurutaḥ.
, adj. (cf. prec.), murderous: niyatam anyonya-˚tiko bhaviṣyati; ˚tikā, subst., = prec.: anyonya-˚kāṃ kartum.
(otherwise unrecorded caus. of Skt. vipraṇaśyati; cf. vipranaṣṭaka), causes or allows to be wasted: mā ca me tvaṃ kiṃcid ato (sc. dravyād) ˚śayiṣyasi (prose).
, maltreats: paro 'pi tāvan nanu rakṣaṇīyaḥ, pāpātmabhir vipratikṛṣyamāṇaḥ (pass.) (vs).

, f. (1) (= Pali vippaṭi˚; cf. next) evil behavior, sin; opp. to pratipatti, q.v.: ˚ti-sthita, see s.v. pratipatti; and, see ib.; ˚ti-duḥkhaṃ (yad dṛṣṭe vā dharme … labhate); vicitrā vineya-kṛtā ˚tiḥ; teṣv (sc. sattveṣu) iha prājñasyāghāto na yuktarūpaḥ, prāg eva ˚tir; mama ˚tiś ca keyam asminn anāgasi (vs), and how could I sin against this innocent one?; (2) (something going wrong, amiss,) mishap, misfortune: mā khalu kumārasya kācid ˚tiḥ, I hope there isnʼt (going to be) some misfortune for the child?

(= Pali vippaṭipajjati; cf. prec. and next), sins: with loc., towards, in regard to, (sattveṣu);; with instr. and sārdhaṃ, sins sexually with:;; (na … bodhisattvasya) sarvacaryāsu vipratipattavyaṃ, must not commit a sin in reference to (sc. find fault with) any actions of a Bodhisattva (see s.v. vimoktavya).
(ppp. to prec.; = Pali vippaṭipanna), sinful: ˚nāś ca bhavanti (leads to retrogression in Bodhisattvas); ārakṣaṇatā ˚neṣu (prose), prob. being on guard with reference to the sinful.
, ppp. (to unrecorded *vi-prati-bandh-; cf. next, also recorded only in BHS), obstructed, in a-vi˚, unobstructed: bodhisattvānām avipratibaddha-sarvavākpathasvabhāvajñānānāṃ.

, (varied? vi-) acquisition: abhāvapratiṣṭhitānabhisaṃskāra-vipratilambhena, by the (varied) acquisition of non-accumulation (of karman) which is established in non-becoming; cf., s.v. anabhisaṃskārika (˚kā).

, m., rarely nt. (= Pali vippaṭi˚; Skt. Lex., once in lit.), discontent with something done or not done (usually, but not always, by oneself) in the past; regret; (especially) remorse:; ˚raḥ; ˚raṃ (n. sg.) saṃjātaṃ (no v.l.); ˚raṃ (n. sg.); mā (so with mss.) bhūc cittasya vipratisāraḥ, I hope you did not feel regret of mind (at having given your breasts); ˚ra-cittam, regretful thought; ˚ra-jāto, characterized by regret;;;;;;;;;. Cf. the next entries, and a-vipratisāra.

, adj. (= prec. = Pali vippaṭi˚; to ˚sāra, and cf. a-vipratisārin), usually regretful of something done or undone in the past by oneself, sometimes an act of generosity, in which case the regret is a sin:, and read vipratisārī, see s.v. pratisārin; often an evil deed or error, or at least failure to perform a good action; then remorseful:, of the boatman who regrets not having ferried the Buddha; satpuruṣā … akuśalena karmaṇā (mss. karmāṇāṃ) vipratisārī (n. pl.) bhavanti, good men … become remorseful for an evil action (or, with mss., for the evil of their actions? misunderstands);;; [Page493-a], read sa vipratisārī; vipratisārībhūtaḥ became regretful, remorseful; ati-vi˚ nātivipratisāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ; sometimes regretful, saddened by circumstances beyond oneʼs control, especially of Māra, saddened by his failure to interfere with the Bodhisattva or Buddha,; vipratisārī usually in this case preceded by duḥkhī durmanā (or ˚no in);;;;;;;; of a devatā, saddened by a kingʼs refusal to heed her warning, duḥkhinī durmanaskā vipratisāriṇī.
, ppp. (=, or perhaps error for, Skt. viprahīṇa), deprived of, free from: pañcāṅga-vi˚, ep. of Buddhas (see aṅga),; but same cpd. with viprahīṇa in same context;; perhaps read so.

(= Pali vipaccanīka; cf. ˚nīya(ka), vipratyayanīya, and a-pratyanīya; cpd. of vi, intensive, and pratyanīka; the forms with -ya(ka) are semi-Pktic, partly no doubt assimilated to suffixal forms in -īya,), antipathetic, opposed, hostile, unwelcome: ˚ka-virodha, hostility between (creatures that are by nature mutually) antipathetic (like snakes and mongooses, cats and mice, as the text explains); (parasparaviruddheṣu …) anyonyadṛṣṭiruci-vipratyanīka-vādiṣu; ˚kaṃ khalu devatānāṃ, contrary (to the ways of men), see which makes clear the true form and mg. of the verse (not understood by); in BHS commonly in cpd. sarvaloka-vi˚, as epithet of dharma- (-paryāya), antipathetic (not acceptable, unwelcome) to the whole (ignorant) world, sometimes accompanied by parallel sarvalokāśraddheya () or ˚kāśraddadhanīya (), not believable by …; with this usage cf. in Pali (sahadhammike vuccamāne, when something in accord with [the Buddhaʼs] dhamma is being said) … vipaccanīka-sātatā, taking delight in contradicting it: so;;;; (in both one ms. ends in ˚ya instead of ˚ka);;.
= prec. and next; I have noted this form only as v.l. (of and two Nep. mss.) for ˚nīka of text in, and v.l. for the same.
= ˚nīya, ˚nīka: (prose) sarvaloka-vi˚ (of dharmaparyāya, as ˚nīka is often used).

, adj. (cf. (= Skt. pramādayati), wastes: (ye ca vaiyāpṛtyakarā vā ārāmikā vā sāṃghikaṃ staupikaṃ vā) dravyaṃ ˚dayanty anayena.
(ppp. to *vi-pra-muṣ-), forgotten, lost (of sacred learning): (taṃ sarvaṃ smarāmy ekapadavyañjanam api) me tato dharmanayān na ˚tam.
